subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Myeloproliferative neoplasms and myelodysplastic syndromes: driver mutations, IPSS-M stratification, hypomethylating agents and JAK inhibition

steps.tx: Classical BCR-ABL1-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms **polycythaemia vera** PV, **essential thrombocythaemia** ET, and **primary myelofibrosis** PMF arise from clonal haematopoietic stem cells. These disorders are driven by mutually exclusive somatic mutations in **JAK2**, **CALR**, or **MPL**, which induce constitutive cytokine-independent downstream JAK-STAT pathway activation and hyperproliferation.

These disorders are driven by mutually exclusive somatic mutations in JAK2, CALR, or MPL, which induce constitutive cytokine-independent downstream JAK-STAT pathway activation and hyperproliferation.

steps.tx: Smear shows **teardrop poikilocytes** with **nucleated red cells** and immature granulocytes, the classic leukoerythroblastic picture of **primary myelofibrosis**. Marrow fibrosis forces blood formation outside the marrow, releasing early forms into circulation. Recognizing this triad points toward a clonal stem cell neoplasm driven by JAK STAT activation.
steps.say: The smear contains many teardrop shaped red cells plus nucleated red cells and immature granulocytes. This combination is termed leukoerythroblastosis and is characteristic of primary myelofibrosis, where scarring of the marrow pushes early blood precursors into the blood. In exams, link teardrop cells with circulating blasts and nucleated red cells to marrow fibrosis from a clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm.

vis.alt: Blood smear shows teardrop cells with nucleated red cells and immature granulocytes.
vis.caption: Teardrop cells with early precursors signal myelofibrosis. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The pathognomonic **JAK2 V617F** point mutation in exon 14 disrupts the regulatory pseudokinase JH2 domain, abolishing autoinhibition and causing constitutive tyrosine kinase activation. Present in over 95% of patients with **polycythaemia vera** and approximately 50% to 60% of individuals with essential thrombocythaemia and primary myelofibrosis, high mutant allele burden correlates with elevated thrombotic risk and fibrotic transformation.

steps.tx: Diagnostic criteria for **polycythaemia vera** mandate fulfilling all three major criteria, or the first two major criteria plus the minor criterion. Major criteria require elevated haemoglobin **over 16.5 g/dL in men** or **16.0 g/dL in women**, bone marrow trilineage panmyelosis, and presence of a JAK2 mutation. The minor criterion is a subnormal serum erythropoietin concentration.
steps.say: Diagnostic criteria for polycythaemia vera mandate fulfilling all three major criteria, or the first two major criteria plus the minor criterion. Major criteria require elevated haemoglobin over sixteen and a half grams in men or sixteen grams in women, bone marrow trilineage panmyelosis, and presence of a JAK2 mutation. The minor criterion is a subnormal serum erythropoietin concentration.

left.title: WHO Major Criteria for PV
points: Hb > 16.5 g/dL (men) or > 16.0 g/dL (women), or Hct > 49% / 48%
Presence of JAK2 V617F or JAK2 exon 12 mutation

right.title: Minor Criterion & Secondary Mimics
points: Causes: Hypoxia, sleep apnoea, smoking, renal tumours
Normal bone marrow morphology in secondary erythrocytosis

steps.tx: In the landmark **CYTO-PV trial**, therapeutic **phlebotomy** maintaining hematocrit strictly **below 45%** combined with daily low-dose aspirin significantly reduced cardiovascular death and major arterial and venous thrombotic events by fourfold. In high-risk polycythaemia vera defined by age 60 years or older or prior thrombosis, adding cytoreductive therapy with hydroxyurea or ropeginterferon alfa-2b is mandatory.

steps.tx: Oral JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor **Ruxolitinib** dramatically improves clinical outcomes in intermediate- and high-risk myelofibrosis. In the pivotal randomized **COMFORT-I and COMFORT-II** clinical trials, ruxolitinib significantly reduced massive **splenomegaly**, alleviated debilitating constitutional symptoms including severe night sweats, pruritus, and fatigue, and significantly prolonged overall survival compared to placebo or best available therapy.

rows: Manage with dose titration; rarely fatal

steps.tx: Heterogeneous clonal stem cell disorders **Myelodysplastic syndromes** MDS are characterized by ineffective haematopoiesis, peripheral blood cytopenias, dysplastic marrow morphology, and elevated risk of transformation into **acute myeloid leukaemia**. Bone marrow biopsy establishes the diagnosis by demonstrating dysplasia in 10% or more cells of one or more myeloid lineages, ring sideroblasts, or elevated myeloblasts under 20%.

Bone marrow biopsy establishes the diagnosis by demonstrating dysplasia in 10% or more cells of one or more myeloid lineages, ring sideroblasts, or elevated myeloblasts under 20%.

left.title: Lower-Risk MDS
points: IPSS-R very low, low, and intermediate <= 3.5
Primary goal: Alleviate cytopenias & transfusion burden

right.title: Higher-Risk MDS
points: High risk of rapid AML transformation
Managed with azacitidine and allogeneic transplant

steps.tx: The updated **Molecular International Prognostic Scoring System** IPSS-M integrates multi-gene somatic mutations across 31 genes with cytogenetic abnormalities and blast counts to refine risk stratification in MDS. Profiling adverse mutations such as **TP53**, ASXL1, RUNX1, and EZH2 reclassifies patients into more precise prognostic categories, identifying candidates who derive survival benefit from early allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

steps.tx: In patients with lower-risk MDS harbouring the **isolated del(5q)** chromosomal abnormality, the immunomodulatory agent **Lenalidomide** induces rapid red blood cell transfusion independence in over 65% of patients. Furthermore, lenalidomide induces complete cytogenetic remissions by selectively degrading casein kinase 1A1 encoded within the 5q deleted chromosomal region, promoting apoptosis of the malignant clone.
